# Turn a Quick Brainstorm into a Clear Meeting Agenda with DeepSeek

> **In short:** Paste your messy meeting notes into DeepSeek and it will draft a structured agenda with time boxes, named owners, and a clear order — usually in under a minute. DeepSeek writes the agenda; it doesn't send invites or book calendars.

We've all had the meeting where ten people arrive with twelve different ideas and leave with no clear next step. This guide walks you through turning that rough brainstorm into a clean, time-boxed agenda that anyone could actually run from. It assumes you've never opened DeepSeek before, and it leans on plain language the whole way. (If "AI chat assistant" is a new phrase: think of DeepSeek as a very fast coworker who reads your notes and writes back structured suggestions — it doesn't store your data after you close the tab on the free plan.)

## Before you start
- **A DeepSeek account** — sign up at the official DeepSeek site with an email or a Google account. The free plan is enough for this task.
- **Phone or laptop with a browser** — the web version works on any modern browser, and the official DeepSeek app is available on iOS and Android.
- **Roughly 10 minutes total** — about 2 minutes to collect your ideas, a minute to paste and wait, and a few minutes to refine.
- **Your raw brainstorm** — bullets, voice-memo transcript, Slack/DM messages, or a photo of scribbles. Anything that captures what should be discussed.

## Step 1 — Collect your meeting ideas in one place
Open your notes app, a blank email, or even a piece of paper, and dump in every topic, question, and decision you want covered. Don't worry about order or wording — just get everything out of your head. If ideas live in different places (a Slack thread, a quick voice memo, an email reply), copy them all into one document so DeepSeek can read them together. If you've been chatting with a colleague about the project, even a rough paraphrase works.
💬 Example: a brainstorm bullet list — "product launch — pricing — who's doing the demo — what is the social plan — we still owe the legal review a reply — vendor contract is stuck — hire for the support role — Q4 OKRs"
You'll know it worked when you have one short document you can highlight and copy in a single swipe.

## Step 2 — Open a fresh DeepSeek chat
In your browser, go to the official DeepSeek site and look for the chat option, or launch the DeepSeek app on your phone. You're aiming for a blank conversation — the kind with an empty input box at the bottom and a "New chat" or sidebar option. Tap that option so the AI starts with a clean slate; older threads can confuse it with rules from previous questions. If you're on mobile, look for a pencil or "New chat" icon in the top corner.
💬 Example: navigate to the official DeepSeek website, choose "Start chat" or "New chat," and confirm the input box is empty.
You'll know it worked when you see an empty chat screen with a text field ready for typing.

## Step 3 — Paste your prompt and ask for the agenda
Click inside the input box and paste your brainstorm, then add a short instruction underneath telling DeepSeek what kind of meeting this is, how long it runs, and who's attending. The more shape you give it, the better the output. Hit the send button — usually a paper-airplane or arrow icon at the right edge of the input box. Wait a few seconds; if you've picked the reasoning-style model, you may see a short "thinking…" block before the answer prints.
💬 Example: "Here are our notes for the meeting. It's a 45-minute weekly product sync on Tuesday with Maria, John, Sarah, and me. Please turn these into a structured agenda with time boxes, topics, and a named owner per item. Notes: product launch, pricing decision, demo owner, social plan, legal review reply, vendor contract, support hire, Q4 OKRs."
You'll know it worked when DeepSeek prints a numbered agenda with names, durations, and clear topics.

## Step 4 — Read the result and ask for adjustments
Now scan the agenda on your screen. Does it cover every point you cared about? Are the time boxes realistic? Is the right person named for each item? If something is off, send a short follow-up message — DeepSeek will rewrite or nudge the agenda in place. Treat it like chatting with a colleague: short, specific notes get better results than vague ones. If the agenda missed a topic entirely, paste that bullet again and ask for it to be added.
💬 Example: "Move the budget review to minute 15, give Priya ownership of the next-step list, and cut the demo recap to two minutes."
You'll know it worked when the second reply matches your team's reality and you can picture running the meeting from it.

## Step 5 — Copy the final agenda into your shared tool
Once the agenda looks right, copy DeepSeek's text (most responses show a copy icon, or you can select it with your finger or mouse) and paste it into the place your team actually reads — a calendar invite description, a Slack message, a Google Doc, or an email. Spend one minute adding your own touches: a one-line welcome, a link to the relevant doc, the meeting link. DeepSeek doesn't send the invite for you, and on the free plan it won't remember this thread next week, so saving it elsewhere matters.
💬 Example: paste the agenda into your meeting invite's description field, then write "Welcome — please read before joining" above it and the meeting link below.
You'll know it worked when the agenda is sitting in your calendar or shared doc, formatted clean, with everything your team needs to walk in prepared.

## Common mistakes
- **Pasting only one or two bullets.** The agenda will feel thin because the AI had nothing to work with. *Fix:* include every topic, even the wishlist ones — DeepSeek can decide what to drop once it sees the full picture.
- **Forgetting to mention who's attending.** Without names, the assistant can't assign owners. *Fix:* drop the list of attendees into the prompt so ownership lands on real people, not "TBD."
- **Skipping the meeting length.** If you don't say "30 minutes" or "60 minutes," DeepSeek will guess and the time boxes may not fit your slot. *Fix:* always include the total duration and the rough priority of each topic.
- **Sending the AI's first draft unchanged.** The output is a starting point, not a finished document. *Fix:* spend two minutes on Step 4 — small edits make the agenda feel owned, not auto-generated.
- **Worrying that DeepSeek is writing the whole meeting.** It's only drafting the plan; the conversation itself is still yours. *Fix:* treat the agenda as a shared script you and your team will run live.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** the same trick works for any get-together — a family holiday plan, a coach's practice schedule, a birthday surprise — because the recipe (dump ideas, ask for structure, refine) is the same everywhere.
- **For your business or work:** instead of starting every meeting from silence or retyping the same template, you get a fresh, customized agenda in under a minute, and the time boxes push your team to leave with real decisions instead of more questions.
- **If you're just getting started:** the simplest move is to run this on your very next meeting — open DeepSeek, paste three bullets and the attendees' names, and see what comes back. The first draft almost always teaches you something about what you actually needed to decide.

## Try it now
Open DeepSeek in a new tab, paste three meeting topics and the names of three attendees, and ask it for a 30-minute agenda with named owners. You'll have a draft in under a minute, and you'll know exactly whether this trick belongs in your weekly workflow.
